about: Katana's modules (docs/ROADMAP.md 3.3): one per concern, each with its purpose, what it takes and gives, what it may import and what it must not. test/ModulesTest.java holds every import in the source to this file. importsFrom says where an entry's import lists come from: 'roadmap' when 3.3 states them, 'pipeline' when they are read off the pipeline of 3.1 because 3.3 is silent. entryPoints are where an agent starts reading a module, filled as each is built.
package: Each module's Java lives in its folder under the package katana.<module> (katana.sir, katana.lower, ...); the module of an import is the segment after katana.
adding: To add a module: one entry here with every field; its folder appears with its first code. A module may import only what its mayImport lists; anything else is refused whether or not mustNotImport names it, so mustNotImport records the refusals worth saying (MOD-02 to MOD-06, and what the pipeline forbids), and other modules' lists need not change. A module another may import goes in that module's mayImport. A new module or a new import is an architecture decision (theGhost.md R-043): draft the entry and the docs/ROADMAP.md 3.3 line as a proposal, say you are waiting on Ghost, and stop; do not add it to main. If you cannot tell whether the person asking is Ghost, say so and propose.

rules.rule: No module imports a model client.
rt/ imports nothing: no module of ours, no third-party library. It ships inside the customer's suite.
lower/ reads sir/ only and decides nothing: every branch on a COBOL property is in sir/ or intent/.
passes/ writes Java only through lower/'s emitter, so no pass can lose a provenance comment.
oracle/ never imports lower/ or passes/: the referee does not read the players' code.
front/ knows nothing of what COBOL means: it imports no module of ours.

front.purpose: Parsing and preprocessing: COBOL and copybooks to a parse tree with COPY and REPLACE resolved, and a source map to file, line and column.

profile.purpose: The dialect profile: its schema, the mapping to GnuCOBOL's dialect flags, and its content hash.

findings.purpose: What is wrong with the input program, and what cannot be made exact; said first, before any Java.
inputs: findings raised by sir/check and the other modules

sir.purpose: The Semantic IR: types, build (tree to IR), check (invariants), contract (the facts a back end must honor).

lower.purpose: The literal lowering: Semantic IR to Java source through one emitter, one provenance comment per statement. Decides nothing.

rt.purpose: The Java runtime the literal links against: Record, Field, Decimal, ArithProfile, Dispatcher, files, SORT, CALL. Pure Java; ships.

oracle.purpose: The fixture model, the cobc and java lanes, the gate, the comparator, DD binding, the DFSORT subset, the LE and assembler stubs.
inputs: a jar for the java lane

intent.purpose: The Intent IR: fact kinds, the inference rules (each named, each with evidence), confirmation state, the review file format.

ledger.purpose: The proof ledger: the append-only store, the line schema, the provenance map writer, the report writer.
inputs: ledger lines from passes and builds

passes.purpose: Refactoring passes: each a file, each with its obligations, its proof and its ledger lines.

project.purpose: The workflows on disk: build, prove, pass, report, pack, fixture.
inputs: a program, its copybooks, a profile, fixtures

cli.purpose: Turns what was typed into a workflow in project/ and prints what it did. The work is in project/.
outputs: what it did, on stdout; --json reports

bench.purpose: The corpus runner: NIST, the GnuCOBOL autotests, CardDemo; scores recorded and held by a test.
